# Agent Brain

<!-- Generated by .github/scripts/generate_documents.py; edit source records instead. -->


## Overview

**Agent Brain** is a custom-owned, vendor-neutral quality bundle for existing coding agents. It contains agent-operating guidance, selectively loaded Agent Skills, and role reference briefs—not a runtime, daemon, proxy, model, or unverified claim of improved benchmark performance.

Build once from canonical sources, distribute platform-native ZIPs for **Codex, Claude Code, Pi, DeepSeek Harness (DSH), and generic AGENTS.md/Agent Skills clients**. The upstream projects referenced in `.agents/bundle/SOURCES.md` supply research ideas, not automatically installed dependencies.

### Get it

Download a host ZIP and `SHA256SUMS` from the [GitHub releases](https://github.com/marius-patrik/agent-brain/releases). Check the filenames of the **actually published** assets: repository changes on `development` are not available as release archives until approved and merged into `main`. Read each archive's `INSTALL.md`; integrate project operating policy separately where a host imports only skills. Host permissions and connected tools remain under the host's control.

### Verification status

Release packaging is tested for reproducibility, manifest shape, file safety, integrity, and platform-specific entrypoints. **No independent agent task-success benchmark has established an uplift.** Host-level installation tests and matched baseline-versus-bundle evaluations must be reported separately with concrete evidence.

See the [bundle distributions](https://github.com/marius-patrik/agent-brain/blob/main/BUNDLES.md) and [benchmark protocol](https://github.com/marius-patrik/agent-brain/blob/main/BENCHMARKS.md).

### Quality and focus capabilities

The original quality/focus candidates cover artifact-specific slop prevention (`quality-without-slop`), **opt-in** action-first replies (`focus-support`), interrupted-task goal continuity (`focus-continuity`), and bounded exploration of high-uncertainty choices (`divergent-ideation`). Creation, evidence and integration capabilities are covered in the following section. They compose with existing review, planning, handoff and delegation skills rather than supplying separate runtimes. Focus-friendly output does not assume a diagnosis, and ideation must respect the host's cost/permission limits.

These skills are compiled from the same canonical catalog. Native installation validation and task-performance benchmarks are different gates; additions to `development` are **not** published until reviewed and merged into `main`.

## Source ownership and layout

| Path | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `.agents/bundle/AGENTS.md` | Canonical **distributed** operating policy |
| `.agents/bundle/bundle.json` | Explicit, sorted list of distributed skills |
| `.agents/bundle/roles/` | Platform-neutral role briefs included as references |

| `.github/scripts/build_bundles.py` | Deterministic host compiler, single owner of packaging |
| `.github/tests/` | Exclusive home of all tests and fixtures |
| `.github/workflows/release.yml` | Tagged asset creation and publication |
| `.agents/requests/`, `.agents/decisions/`, `.agents/notes/`, `.agents/rules/` | Reviewed sources of project PRD, architecture, README and contributor guide |
| `.agents/GOAL.md`, `.agents/PLAN.md`, `.agents/TODO.md` | Authoritative goal and active work state |
| `repo.dfconfig` | DarkFactory integration and GitHub policy declaration |
| `.darkfactory` | Pinned DarkFactory development-tooling submodule, not distributed |

Root README and CONTRIBUTING are symlinks to generated documents; generated Markdown is not a second editable source. Agent Brain distributions never package DarkFactory or the repository's own generated project rules.

## Develop, validate and release

Changes begin on a dedicated branch against `development`. Update approved requirements and accepted decisions with a meaningful scope change, edit canonical skill sources, then regenerate projections. PRs to `main` must originate from `development` and are created by the GitHub Actions bot to permit independent owner review. The repository setting allowing Actions pull-request creation is enabled; the bot-authored promotion PR has been observed. Native `main` protection is also enabled. These administrative gates do **not** approve or merge the PR: independent human approval and green current-head checks remain necessary before publishing. Preserve review and CI gates.

```bash
python3 .github/scripts/generate_documents.py --write
python3 .github/scripts/generate_documents.py --check
python3 .github/scripts/build_bundles.py --tag v0.0.0 --check
python3 -m unittest discover -s .github/tests -p 'test_*.py'
```

The repository uses **Git-tag-derived SemVer**, with no required `VERSION` file. A successful push to `main` publishes platform ZIPs and checksum file in its GitHub Release. The release workflow checks that the tag points to the merged commit, downloads the published ZIPs and SHA256SUMS, and independently compares all six remote assets byte-for-byte with the locally validated release build. Never replace an earlier release's content silently.

For skill changes, justify the trigger, run regression and negative-trigger cases, and record evidence. Structural packaging tests do not prove skill usefulness.

_Source: [0003-contribution.md](notes/0003-contribution.md)_


## Repository governance

The `main` branch must be protected through live GitHub settings. Configuration declarations and CI workflows alone cannot enforce branch protection. An authenticated repository administrator can audit and apply the policy with:

```bash
python3 .github/scripts/apply_branch_protection.py
python3 .github/scripts/apply_branch_protection.py --apply
```

The **Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions → Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests** setting is enabled. Native `main` branch protection has been independently observed as active, with required `main-source`/`generated-docs` checks, one approving review, required conversation resolution, strict up-to-date checks and no force-push or deletion. The [bot-authored promotion PR #19](https://github.com/marius-patrik/agent-brain/pull/19) exists; the release remains pending until the required owner review, protected merge and resulting release-asset verification. See [issue #14](https://github.com/marius-patrik/agent-brain/issues/14).

## Installation and runtime boundaries

Each release archive contains a standard skills root, a host-specific manifest or directory layout, `INSTALL.md`, a source manifest, and the repository license. The bundle supplies **instructions only**, not credentials, executable third-party plugins, private services, or agent orchestration.

Claude Code and Codex plugin installation does not automatically install a project-specific `AGENTS.md` policy. In Claude Code, create `CLAUDE.md` in the consumer project (rather than in the plugin root) if that project should import `@AGENTS.md`. Pi package installation loads the declared skills; project policy is a separate step. DSH loads its project `.agents/skills` root when the filesystem skill provider and registry are mounted. Generic Open Agents-compatible consumers load project `AGENTS.md` and skills if supported.

`.github/` is an actual Git directory for repository CI and release; the pinned `.darkfactory` submodule is development tooling and is not copied into the output archives.

_Source: [0005-darkfactory-structure.md](notes/0005-darkfactory-structure.md)_


## Creation quality, evidence and low-friction execution

Agent Brain adds four distinct creation/evidence procedures alongside its existing quality and focus candidates: `interface-craft` develops usable flows, `change-resilience` protects multi-step extension paths, `source-fidelity` checks claims against sources, and `contract-first-integration` reconciles APIs and state owners **before** coordinated implementation. They do not replace independent review or behavioral testing.

`focus-support` remains opt-in and can expose one executable starting action while preserving requested technical depth. `focus-continuity` uses the existing project plan and handoff to recover the exact next step after interruptions, without retaining health-related details or starting background work.

These are authored procedures, **not measured performance improvements**. Controlled external validation remains necessary.

_Source: [0006-creation-quality.md](notes/0006-creation-quality.md)_
